panels.title: Chat turn latency over time
panels.description: One point per live/eval run_chat_turn call (the full decide_tools -> execute_tools -> generate_answer chain), from MLflow's own trace_info table -- not a synthetic metric, the actual wall-clock duration MLflow recorded for that call, color-split by OK/ERROR. A cluster of ERROR points at ~60000ms is the Ollama client's hardcoded timeout (app/extraction/ollama_client.py's _TIMEOUT_SECONDS) firing, not a crash.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_timestamp(timestamp_ms / 1000.0) AS time,
  execution_time_ms AS latency_ms,
  status
FROM trace_info
WHERE experiment_id = (SELECT experiment_id FROM experiments WHERE name = 'jme-chatbot-rag')
  AND trace_name = '_run_chat_turn'
  AND $__unixEpochFilter(timestamp_ms / 1000)
ORDER BY timestamp_ms

panels.title: Error rate (selected time range)
panels.description: Share of run_chat_turn calls (live chat page + eval harness) that errored, usually the Ollama client's 60s timeout under load -- see the latency panel above for exactly which calls.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'ERROR') / greatest(count(*), 1), 1) AS error_pct
FROM trace_info
WHERE experiment_id = (SELECT experiment_id FROM experiments WHERE name = 'jme-chatbot-rag')
  AND trace_name = '_run_chat_turn'
  AND $__unixEpochFilter(timestamp_ms / 1000)

panels.title: P50 / P95 / avg latency by model (LLM spans)
panels.description: Per-call Ollama/vLLM generate() latency broken out by model_name -- MLflow's spans table already tracks this per LLM-type span (app/extraction/ollama_client.py's generate()/embed(), @mlflow.trace(span_type=SpanType.LLM)), so this is the real per-model decode speed, not an estimate. Useful for comparing the live 1.5b default against any larger model tried via the eval harness's model-size knob.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  s.model_name,
  count(*) AS n_calls,
  round(avg(s.duration_ns / 1e6)::numeric, 0) AS avg_ms,
  round((percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.duration_ns / 1e6))::numeric, 0) AS p50_ms,
  round((percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.duration_ns / 1e6))::numeric, 0) AS p95_ms
FROM spans s
JOIN trace_info ti ON ti.request_id = s.trace_id
WHERE ti.experiment_id = (SELECT experiment_id FROM experiments WHERE name = 'jme-chatbot-rag')
  AND s.type = 'LLM'
  AND $__unixEpochFilter(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000)
GROUP BY s.model_name
ORDER BY n_calls DESC

panels.title: Recent chat requests (session / user / latency / status)
panels.description: Per-request traceability: which chat session and role asked what, how long it took, and whether it errored -- tagged by app/chatbot/graph.py's _tag_current_trace() (session_id as MLflow's own session_id column, role via the mlflow.trace.user convention, the question text as a 'question' tag). Click a row's trace in the MLflow UI (http://localhost:5000) for the full span breakdown (tool calls, prompt/completion tokens, per-call duration).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_timestamp(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000.0) AS time,
  ti.session_id,
  trm.value AS role,
  ti.status,
  ti.execution_time_ms AS latency_ms,
  tt.value AS question
FROM trace_info ti
LEFT JOIN trace_request_metadata trm ON trm.request_id = ti.request_id AND trm.key = 'mlflow.trace.user'
LEFT JOIN trace_tags tt ON tt.request_id = ti.request_id AND tt.key = 'question'
WHERE ti.experiment_id = (SELECT experiment_id FROM experiments WHERE name = 'jme-chatbot-rag')
  AND ti.trace_name = '_run_chat_turn'
  AND $__unixEpochFilter(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000)
ORDER BY ti.timestamp_ms DESC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Guardrail triggers (selected time range)
panels.description: How many run_chat_turn calls were blocked/redacted by app/chatbot/guardrails.py (contact_detail_request, injection, rate_limited, output_pii_redacted, capacity_limit, llm_unavailable -- tagged on the trace as guardrail_triggered). A sustained non-zero rate here is a real signal worth looking at: either genuine abuse/scraping attempts, or a false-positive pattern worth refining the guardrail's rules for.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS triggers
FROM trace_info ti
JOIN trace_tags tt ON tt.request_id = ti.request_id AND tt.key = 'guardrail_triggered'
WHERE ti.experiment_id = (SELECT experiment_id FROM experiments WHERE name = 'jme-chatbot-rag')
  AND $__unixEpochFilter(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000)

panels.title: Guardrail triggers by type over time
panels.description: Same trigger events as the stat panel, broken out by reason (contact_detail_request / injection / rate_limited / output_pii_redacted / capacity_limit / llm_unavailable) over time -- a spike in one specific reason points at what to investigate first.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('hour', to_timestamp(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000.0)) AS time,
  tt.value AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM trace_info ti
JOIN trace_tags tt ON tt.request_id = ti.request_id AND tt.key = 'guardrail_triggered'
WHERE ti.experiment_id = (SELECT experiment_id FROM experiments WHERE name = 'jme-chatbot-rag')
  AND $__unixEpochFilter(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Recent guardrail-triggered requests (session / role / reason / question)
panels.description: Per-event detail for audit: which session/role triggered which guardrail, on what question -- the actual rows to read for abuse investigation or false-positive tuning, not just the aggregate counts above.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_timestamp(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000.0) AS time,
  ti.session_id,
  trm.value AS role,
  tt.value AS guardrail_triggered,
  tq.value AS question
FROM trace_info ti
JOIN trace_tags tt ON tt.request_id = ti.request_id AND tt.key = 'guardrail_triggered'
LEFT JOIN trace_request_metadata trm ON trm.request_id = ti.request_id AND trm.key = 'mlflow.trace.user'
LEFT JOIN trace_tags tq ON tq.request_id = ti.request_id AND tq.key = 'question'
WHERE ti.experiment_id = (SELECT experiment_id FROM experiments WHERE name = 'jme-chatbot-rag')
  AND $__unixEpochFilter(ti.timestamp_ms / 1000)
ORDER BY ti.timestamp_ms DESC
LIMIT 200
